payload.subject: Planning perspective: in-memory subagents stay host-side
payload.summary:
Planning note from Codex: In-memory subagents should stay host-side. They are a host execution strategy, not a Rally responsibility. Pi can run child agents inside Pi; Claude can use Agent/Task; Codex can use native delegation or managed sessions. Rally should remain the facilitator: record facts, check boundaries, route handoffs, expose room state, and give high-level coordination guidance.

Product direction: Agent Rally Point should enable coordination for 100s of agents across harnesses, worktrees, terminals, and hosts. That requires durable shared state and visible boundaries, not a parent process holding child-agent state in RAM.

Planning implication: dynamic-workflows/ should be a portable protocol + guardrail module: workstream descriptor, MECE task packets, validation/output requirements, deterministic/literal descriptor linting, and host-facing skills. Do not port Pi SessionManager, Node VM workflow executor, in-memory subagent lifecycle, Pi TUI/tool plumbing, or new rally workflow execution subcommands.

Tiering: in-memory subagents are allowed as Tier 1 host-native fan-out behind a host adapter. Tier 2 cross-host work uses rally run/inject and scoped handoffs. Rally coordinates; hosts execute. For weaker coding harnesses, Rally can provide more guidance through skills, protocol docs, task-packet linting, and suggested commands, while still not becoming the executor.
